Celtic went out at this stage last year, drawing a blank against Kairat Almaty after failing to sign a proven striker. The arrival of Durán and Høgh solved that problem but other signings were slow to come and the German midfielder Mika Baur was handed a start in his Celtic Park debut.

The 22-year-old’s inclusion was necessitated by the departure of Arne Engels to West Ham at the weekend, which caused more anxiety among Celtic fans who have seen their team fail in their last five Champions League qualifying campaigns. The playoff defeat against the Kazakhstan side followed losses in earlier rounds against AEK Athens, Cluj, Ferencvaros and Midtjylland in recent seasons.

The Celtic fans were in full voice in the buildup but there were early worries. Moses Usor sent a brilliant volley into the top corner inside 30 seconds but was flagged offside, before Samuel Adeniran scuffed a shot wide when clean through.

The Lask forward soon forced a save from Viljami Sinisalo with Celtic looking very open in central midfield without Engels, but Durán threatened twice from half-chances before Nygren opened the scoring.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Benjamin Nygren puts Celtic ahead in their Champions League playoff against Lask. Photograph: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock

Lask had a headed goal chalked off for offside before Durán struck his first and Sinisalo made another couple of saves before the break.

The Celtic captain, Callum McGregor, fired a deflected 20-yard shot off the inside of a post as chances kept coming in the second half, and Usor squandered two excellent opportunities.

Reo Hatate came on to huge acclaim in what could be one of his final Celtic Park appearances before Durán came close twice from long range before his second goal of the night.

The goal hero got another massive cheer for sprinting back to his own byline to make a challenge and Sinisalo continued to look assured as Celtic maintained their clean sheet.

Sports.title: Ligue 1 forced to take drastic action as PSG pitch deemed ‘unplayable’ days before opener
Sports.content:
Ligue 1 forced to take drastic action as PSG pitch deemed ‘unplayable’ days before opener

Paris Saint-Germain have been forced to play their opening game of the Ligue 1 season away from the Parc des Princes.

The French champions' home match against Rennes will switch stadiums due to a fungus outbreak on the pitch.



1 PSG have had to have their season opener moved after a pitch assessment Credit: AFP

It will now be played at Rennes' Roazhon Park instead on Sunday evening, with the surface deemed to be unsafe.

PSG confirmed the change following an assessment of the pitch conditions by the Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP).

The Parc des Princes' pitch was said to be 'particularly damaged' due to the recent heatwave and the conditions have made it unplayable with regard to player welfare.



The game will stay as an 8:45pm kick-off local time (7:45pm in the UK) on Sunday, but PSG will now be the away side.

PSG statement

Revealing the news of the enforced change, PSG wrote: "The latest heatwave, following the successive and exceptional heatwaves that hit the Paris region this summer, has greatly accelerated the deterioration of the pitch at the Parc des Princes, which is now particularly damaged just days before the match between Paris Saint-Germain and Stade Rennais, scheduled for Sunday, August 23 at 8:45 p.m. as part of the first day of Ligue 1.



"In light of this situation, the Professional Football League (LFP), in conjunction with Paris Saint-Germain, conducted an assessment of the pitch conditions.

"This assessment concluded that the current conditions did not allow the match to be held under satisfactory circumstances, particularly with regard to the safety and physical well-being of the players, which remain the absolute priority.



"In order to allow the match to take place on the date and at the time originally planned, it has therefore been decided, in agreement with the LFP and Stade Rennais, that it will take place in Rennes, at Roazhon Park, on Sunday, August 23 at 8:45 p.m.

"Paris Saint-Germain fully understands the inconvenience caused by this change for its supporters and all those who had planned to attend this match at the Parc des Princes.

"The Club regrets this exceptional situation and will communicate all information regarding applicable procedures to ticket holders as soon as possible. "

The Champions League winners also thank Rennes for making the match possible and hosting at their home stadium instead.



However, it has been reported that Rennes were reluctant to host the fixture as they don't want to overload their pitch.

Meanwhile, PSG announced that plans have been made to replace the pitch at Parc des Princes ahead of their next home game, which will be against Monaco on September 4.

What happens to the reverse fixture?

Reports in France state that the reverse fixture in March 2027 will still be played at Roazhon Park and not in Paris.

Therefore, it is expected that both matches between PSG and Rennes are going to be played at the latter's stadium.



But the possibility remains that Luis Enrique's side may not be pleased with playing an extra away game this season.

So, the LFP may face a conundrum at the start of next year when the reverse fixture comes around.

Sports.title: Inter Milan to be transformed by three England internationals as new-look starting XI revealed
Sports.content:
Inter Milan to be transformed by three England internationals as new-look starting XI revealed

Inter Milan head into 2026/27 with a raft of new signings as they look to defend their Serie A title.

Former Inter defender Cristian Chivu guided the Nerazzurri to their 21st Scudetto in his first full season as head coach, as well as lifting the Coppa Italia for a domestic double.

5 Ex-Romania international Chivu previously coached Inter's youth sides Credit: Getty

Having gone through pre-season unbeaten, wrapping things up with a 1-0 win over Real Betis, Inter begin the new Serie A campaign at home to Monza on Saturday.

Also in the Champions League for the ninth straight campaign, Inter will find out their European opponents when the draw for the league phase of the competition takes place next Thursday (August 27).

And with plenty of new faces through the door at the San Siro this summer – as well as a number of big names leaving at the end of their contracts – Chivu's starting XI could have quite a different look to it.

Inter's English influx

With the exception of veteran midfielder Henrikh Mkhitaryan, who will miss the season opener through suspension, Inter have a full squad at their disposal.

That includes three new English signings: John Stones, Djed Spence – both of whom starred at the 2026 World Cup – and fellow international Curtis Jones.

Stones has joined on a free transfer after leaving Manchester City, with Spence arriving from Tottenham and Jones set to complete a switch from Liverpool.

And European football expert Andy Brassell thinks the trio could thrive at Inter.

Stones, Spence and Jones' new adventure

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, he explained: "Stones is a great opportunity and feels like someone in the kind of Ashley Young mould, really."

Former Manchester United and England full-back Young spent 18 months at Inter, helping them to the 2020/21 Serie A title.

"Of course, a very different type of player, but Young got a great couple of extra years at elite level there and did great really at Inter," Brassell continued.

5 Stones brings a wealth of Premier League and Champions League experience to Inter Credit: Getty

"I think with Stones, a little bit like Rodri, if you take a lot of the extra physical pressure off him, he becomes the footballer he should have been all along again.

"Because he's struggled in recent times, even though he's got all the ability in the world and we know that on his days he's as good as he gets. So if that works for Inter, then great. They'll have had a great pick-up there.

"Spence is super important because they need that energy and that nous that he really has in the wing-back position.

"He's younger than [Denzel] Dumfries [who has left for Real Madrid]. I think he could be a really great signing for them.

"As well, he can cover [Federico] Dimarco on the other side. Dimarco doesn't need to get overplayed as well. He needs to have a little bit of a look at his minutes. So Spence is going to be super important."

Alluding to Jones, he added: "And I do think they've needed to make the midfield younger over the last couple of years, and they've made moves towards doing that. That was something that they spoke about at length last summer, about making themselves younger.

5 Spence impressed in England's run to the World Cup semi-finals, playing alongside Stones on a number of occasions Credit: Getty

5 Jones has scored 22 goals in 228 appearances for boyhood club Liverpool, winning two Premier League titles Credit: Getty

"I think Spence and Jones put together, you look at their age and their athleticism, it's clear what direction Inter are trying to move into.

"It's a great opportunity for them both of course because they've got the opportunity to compete for Serie A and to go far in the Champions League."

How will Inter line up this season?

One would expect Inter to continue in Chivu's favoured 3-5-2 formation which he deployed to great effect last term and during pre-season.

Between the sticks, ex-Lazio goalkeeper Ivan Provedel has come in as the successor to the departing Yann Sommer.

Manuel Akanji is likely to sit at the heart of the back three, having made his loan move from Man City permanent, with his old teammate Stones to the right and Alessandro Bastoni to the left.

The right and left wing-back positions look set to be occupied by Spence and Dimarco respectively, either side of a midfield three comprising Hakan Calhanoglu, Jones and Nicolo Barella.

And in attack, it's likely to be a front two of Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martinez, who scored 40 goals between them in all competitions last season.

Sports.title: Two England starlets tipped to claim Premier League prize as individual awards predicted for 2026/27 season
Sports.content:
Roll up, roll up! It's time for the talkSPORT 2026/27 Premier League Awards... well, predictions.

Jeff Stelling and Ally McCoist have selected who they believe are set to stand out as the best of the best in the new season, which begins live on talkSPORT on Friday when Arsenal host Coventry City.



10 Arsenal will return to the Premier League as holders Credit: Getty

Some of the best players in world football are ready and raring to go after a busy summer of World Cup action.

Erling Haaland will be eyeing his fourth Golden Boot in five seasons at Manchester City, while Declan Rice hopes to be the midfield marshal in another title-winning side with Arsenal.

There have also been nine new managerial appointments across the 20 clubs, all of whom will be desperate for strong debut campaigns.



Andoni Iraola has swapped Bournemouth for Liverpool, Enzo Maresca is now at City and former Premier League star Xabi Alonso has taken charge at Chelsea.

On Breakfast, Stelling and McCoist went through five categories and predicted some big names to claim individual accolades this season, including two England starlets for Young Player of the Year.



Player of the Season

McCoist - "It's tough, isn't it? Tough. I tried to predict... you look at the teams that will do well, it doesn't necessarily mean the Player of the Season is going to come from there but I think there's a higher chance that they will come from there.

"I think Arsenal will have another great season, not just for the fact of the way they played at the weekend but adding to that, the players that they have brought into the squad have indeed strengthened them.



"I think Declan Rice will have another fantastic season. I think (Martin) Odegaard coming off a great World Cup...

"There will be slight question marks against those two, and probably (Bukayo) Saka as well, how they handle the season after the World Cup, and whether any fatigue sets in... I'm going Saka. I think Saka will have a magnificent season on the right-hand side for Arsenal."

Stelling - "You look at strikers, you've got to. I think (Alexander) Isak has got to have a better season than Haaland again.

10 McCoist has tipped Saka to be the best player in the new season Credit: Getty



10 For Stelling, it's his Arsenal teammate and captain Odegaard Credit: Getty

"But, I'm going Martin Odegaard, because I thought he had a great World Cup and he's started this season in the Community Shield brilliantly.

"If he's back to the player he was a couple of seasons ago... oh my goodness, love him."

Manager of the Season

McCoist - "I'm taking Arsenal to win it, so the obvious answer would be (Mikel) Arteta, but I must mention one or two others. Do you know who I'm expecting big things from? (Nottingham) Forest, Oliver Glasner.



"I think he'll do well... I think they've got a lot of things going for them, I think he did an unbelievable job at (Crystal) Palace and I think Palace will clearly miss him, although the new fella's got to be given a chance.

"I think Forest will do okay this year, I think Glasner will get a mention. The rest of them will be interesting to see. I think any of the promoted clubs, if they keep them in the division (deserve a shout)...

"I think out of the teams, I think Coventry (have the best chance)... I think it was maybe said in the betting, Ipswich are the biggest favourites to stay up. I think Coventry might have the best chance. If they stay up, Frank (Lampard) will come into the running."

10 Arteta could win back-to-back Manager of the Season titles Credit: Getty



10 Alonso will hope to be a big success in the Chelsea dugout Credit: Getty

Stelling - "I agree... I think that (Roberto) De Zerbi could have a fantastic season (at Tottenham Hotspur). I think Daniel Farke could have a great season at Leeds as well.

"But, I'm going to go with Xabi Alonso (at Chelsea). If he needs to prove himself again, then I think he will at Stamford Bridge."

Young Player of the Season

McCoist - "Interesting. I think Nico O'Reilly has been fantastic (at City), he'll come into the equation. I'm expecting massive improvement and more consistency from Florian Wirtz (at Liverpool).



"Adam Wharton is a player I really enjoy watching (at Palace), I think he's a terrific passer of the ball. You watch him, ball comes to him, first thing he does is look forward. If you're a forward playing with Adam Wharton, you're in heaven because he'll find you, fire it into your feet or fire it in behind.

"But, Rio Ngumoha at Liverpool, I am really looking forward to seeing him... I'm not going to say for a minute he was kind of held back by (Mohamed) Salah, because Salah is one of the best players the league has ever seen.

"But he was a player I wanted to see more of and I think we'll see more of him next season, and he'll light the place up again."

Stelling - "For me... look, there hasn't been much to shout about for Newcastle in pre-season. But, I think this could be a big season for Lewis Miley.



"I really, really like him... he was forced to play full-back at times last season. But he's a midfield player, and I love him."

10 Ngumoha may become the Premier League's shining starlet Credit: Getty

10 Stelling has backed Miley for another strong season at Newcastle Credit: Getty

Top Scorer of the Season

Stelling - "Well, this should be pretty straightforward, shouldn't it?"



McCoist - "You're expecting improvement, massive things from Isak. (Igor) Thiago had a brilliant season last season (at Brentford)...

Stelling - "There's only one name, though... has to be Erling Haaland. Even if they finish seventh, as Pearcey (Stuart Pearce) thinks they will, it's still going to be Erling Haaland."

10 It will take a lot to beat Haaland for the top scorer title this season Credit: AFP

Signing of the Season

McCoist - "Do you know who I think will do well? He didn't play particularly well at the weekend... I'm still expecting big things from Elliot Anderson.



"He kind of played in the right-hand side position at the weekend. I wouldn't say he looked lost, there was nothing going for Manchester City at the weekend at all. I still think he will have a fantastic season."

Stelling - "For me, it's another big money signing. I think Chelsea are going to have a good season so, for me, Morgan Rogers. We didn't see the best of him at the World Cup because he wasn't playing...

"I mean, look, it could easily be Danny Welbeck as well, by the way, that could be a brilliant signing. But Morgan Rogers, for me. I think he's just a fantastic footballer."

10 McCoist thinks Anderson will be worth the £116m price tag Credit: Getty

Sports.title: Chelsea set for cash windfall as Strasbourg receive record sale fee for star
Sports.content:
Chelsea set for cash windfall as Strasbourg receive record sale fee for star

Ex-Chelsea winger Diego Moreira has completed a £56million move from Strasbourg to AC Milan.

The 22-year-old has penned a five-year deal that sees him join Ruben Amorim's side in a club-record sale for Strasbourg.

5 Moreira has signed a five-year deal through to 2031 at the San Siro Credit: Getty

The exit fee smashes the Ligue 1 side's previous record departure of £30m, which saw Dilane Bakwa join Nottingham Forest last summer.

Moreira's move comes just two years after Chelsea sold the Belgian international to their sister club for a fee of £1.7m.

However, the Blues are in line to benefit from his latest transfer, as talkSPORT understands they are set for a cash windfall.

A sell-on clause is understood to have been included in the wide man's Stamford Bridge departure in 2024.

As a result, Chelsea can expect a meaningful sell-on fee, although the exact percentage is not currently clear.

Remarkable transformation

Few would've expected Moreira to command such a huge fee when he left Stamford Bridge after a forgettable year in west London.

He joined the Blues from Benfica on a free transfer in 2023 but struggled to make an impact in the capital.

Moreira made just one senior appearance for Chelsea, coming off the bench in a Carabao Cup win over AFC Wimbledon, and also spent time on loan at Lyon.

But after swapping London for Strasbourg in 2024, the four-cap Belgium international has since rebuilt his career.

Under the management of Liam Rosenior, he established himself as a highly-rated attacking talent.

5 Moreira left Chelsea without making a Premier League appearance Credit: Getty

5 But the Belgian then enjoyed a resurgence under Liam Rosenior at Strasbourg Credit: AFP

The versatile wide man was an ever-present in his first year in France, making 32 league appearances as Strasbourg finished seventh, which earned Conference League qualification.

Moreira's improved form continued last term, even after Rosenior's ill-fated departure to Chelsea in January.

He featured 42 times in all competitions, scoring five times in an historic campaign, as Strasbourg reached their first ever European semi-final before being beaten by Rayo Vallecano in the last four of the Conference League.

But after completing his big-money move to AC Milan, Moreira will have another opportunity to test himself in Europe.

Now managed by ex-Manchester United boss Amorim, his side will compete in the Europa League in the upcoming campaign, having qualified via a fifth-place Serie A finish last term.

The Italian giants will fancy their chances in the competition, with Moreira their latest statement signing this summer.

5 Amorim was appointed AC Milan boss in June, six months after being sacked by Man United Credit: Getty

Goncalo Ramos has also arrived from Paris Saint-Germain for a reported club record transfer fee of about £60m.

'One of the best'

One man who won't be surprised by Moreira's record-breaking move is European football expert Andy Brassell.

The journalist highlighted the ex-Chelsea man's rising stock at Strasbourg in October 2025, insisting he had made huge progress.

Brassell told talkSPORT: “Diego Moreira, who was formerly at Chelsea, has really been transformed under Rosenior.

“He was someone who went out from Chelsea on loan to Lyon, looked absolutely nowhere near ready for top-flight football.

“Then a year later, he goes to Strasbourg, and all of a sudden, he's one of the best wing-backs in the league because he changes his position.

5 Moreira leaves Strasbourg having scored seven goals in 76 appearances Credit: Getty

“He's so good, not just with the ball, but without the ball as well. His defensive awareness is fantastic now.

“In terms of scoring and creating, the runs he makes, the awareness that he's got when Strasbourg are out of possession, all of those parts of his games, really, Rosenior has absolutely transformed him. It's amazing.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa consider moves for Tosin Adarabioyo and six-cap England player as replacement for Ezri Konsa
Sports.content:
Aston Villa consider moves for Tosin Adarabioyo and six-cap England player as replacement for Ezri Konsa

Aston Villa have placed defenders Tosin Adarabioyo and Fikayo Tomori on their list of transfer targets, talkSPORT understands.

The pair have been identified as potential replacements for the departing Ezri Konsa.



3 Villa are considering a move for Tosin as they eye a replacement for Konsa Credit: Getty

Villa are preparing for life without the England centre-back, who is closing in on a move to Arsenal.

The Gunners have agreed a deal in principle worth in excess of £50million with their Premier League rivals.

Konsa is now set to undergo a medical with Arsenal on Thursday before completing his switch.



Ahead of his exit, Villa are now looking to bring in a replacement to restore their central defensive options.

Villa eye Tosin and Tomori

Amongst their targets is Chelsea's Tosin, who has previously been eyed by Benfica this summer.



The 28-year-old's Stamford Bridge future is currently unclear after he was stripped of his squad number by the club.

Tosin previously wore the No.4 shirt, which has now been handed to new signing Valentin Barco.



Meanwhile, the former Fulham man has been left with the No.38 shirt for the upcoming campaign.

Tosin, who has less than two years remaining on his current deal, joined the club from the Cottagers on a free transfer in 2024.

Last season saw the former England youth international make 16 Premier League appearances during a campaign disrupted by hamstring and calf injuries.

3 Tomori is also a centre-back target for Villa after he was transfer listed by Milan Credit: Getty



Villa are also weighing up a move for Tomori, who has been transfer listed after entering the final year of his deal at AC Milan.

The Chelsea academy graduate joined the Italian giants in 2021 after impressing on loan at the San Siro.

Tomori, who has been capped six times by the Three Lions, made 17 Premier League appearances for the Blues before moving to Milan.

He has since won a Serie A title and an Italian Super Cup during his time at the club.



Villa transfer plans

A new centre-back is a priority for Villa, with Konsa's departure set to leave Unai Emery with limited options in the position.

Pau Torres, Victor Lindelof and Tyrone Mings are amongst just four recognised central defenders at his disposal.

3 Konsa is set to undergo a medical with Arsenal after a fee was agreed with Villa Credit: Getty

The quartet is completed by Modou Keba Cisse, a 21-year-old signed from Austrian champions LASK earlier this summer.



Cisse is one of six new signings to arrive at Villa Park already this summer.

It follows the additions of goalkeeper Zion Suzuki from Parma and Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri on Thursday.

They have joined fellow new signings Joao Gomes, Johan Manzambi and Alejandro Garnacho at the club.

Villa begin the new season away to Brighton on Sunday, with kick-off at 2pm.



Unfortunately for Villa supporters, though, Garnacho is a doubt to face the Seagulls, whilst Gomes and Manzambi have been ruled out.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sends thank you note to Jamie Carragher after Liverpool legend’s X-rated reaction to Gary Neville
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford sends thank you note to Jamie Carragher after Liverpool legend’s X-rated reaction to Gary Neville

Marcus Rashford found an unexpected saviour in Jamie Carragher after he shut down Gary Neville's attempts to talk about him.

Rashford is back at Old Trafford after his dream permanent move to Barcelona failed to materialise, and looks set to be a Manchester United player again this season after making his return on the pitch.



4 Rashford made his first Man United appearance in 20 months against AC Milan on Saturday Credit: Getty

The 28-year-old made his first appearance for his boyhood club for almost two years against AC Milan on Saturday.

With the Red Devils falling to a 4-2 defeat in their final pre-season friendly, Rashford came on to log his first minutes for the club since December 2024.

After loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona, the England star has now been welcomed back by manager Michael Carrick.



It represents a dramatic turnaround for Rashford, whose United career looked to be over when he left to join Villa on loan in January 2025 after being frozen out by former boss Ruben Amorim.

Touchy subject

With Rashford's return to Man United a major talking point this summer, it was a fiery topic of discussion on The Overlap.



In a clip from an upcoming episode of the podcast, Neville tries to raise the subject, only to be shot down by co-host Carragher.

The Man United legend begins: "Marcus Rashford, what do we think? Last question."



Visibly annoyed, Carragher responds: "Oh f****** hell! Can we do a podcast without mentioning Rashford? Stop it! Oh my God.

"It’s like the Trent [Alexander-Arnold] and Rashford [podcast]. There was like a little part of the podcast - the Trent part or the Rashford part."

Neville then jokingly quips: "How is Trent?", to which Carragher replies: "Oh my God!"

4 Rashford returned to the United fold wearing the No.9 jersey against AC Milan, and Neville was keen to discuss his comeback Credit: Getty



Trying to clarify his choice to bring up Rashford, Neville continues: "No, but he’s come back to United."

But Carragher was having none of this, firing back: "So what? Oh my God. He’s just a good player for Man United!"

Rashford responds

Carragher and Neville's interaction quickly began to circulate online, and eventually found its way to Rashford himself.

And the forward was quick to thank Liverpool icon Carragher for sticking up for him, as he gave a pointed response on social media.



He wrote on X: "Thanks, Jamie.

"It would be great to be able to get my head down and play football without my name being mentioned every day," followed by a crying emoji.

4 Rashford and Carragher saw eye-to-eye about Neville's attempts to discuss the England star Credit: Getty

With Man United just days away from their Premier League opener against newly-promoted Hull, few would have expected to see Rashford involved at the start of the summer.

However, after spending last season on loan at Barcelona, the Englishman saw his hopes of joining them permanently fall apart when England teammate Anthony Gordon completed a £70million move from Newcastle to the Camp Nou.



With a move elsewhere not materialising since then, United boss Carrick now appears buoyed by the prospect of Rashford staying at the club.

Carrick said during pre-season: "He's our player, you know, and he's come back great. He's just like any other player.

"I've known Marcus a long time and, you know, he gives us something a little bit different. He's been in great spirits since he's been back.

"He's been back two or three days training and it's just pretty normal, to be honest.



4 Michael Carrick has spoken positively about the reintegration of his old Man United teammate Rashford Credit: Getty

"We're looking forward to the start of the season."

Sports.title: Joao Pedro takes No.9 jersey off Liam Delap as Chelsea confirm multiple squad number changes
Sports.content:
Joao Pedro takes No.9 jersey off Liam Delap as Chelsea confirm multiple squad number changes

Chelsea have made changes to squad numbers in their playing side with Joao Pedro taking Liam Delap's jersey.

The Brazilian striker has been named the club's new No.9 ahead of the new campaign with Delap settling for No.12.



3 Pedro is Chelsea's new No.9 after the Blues confirmed their squad numbers Credit: Getty

It comes after Pedro was named the Blues' Player of the Year last season following 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions.

The 24-year-old previously wore the No.9 jersey for Brighton during his time on the south coast.

Chelsea squad number changes

His switch from No.20, which he had worn following his arrival from the Seagulls last summer, has seen Delap, who has been linked with a move away from Stamford Bridge this summer, stripped of his squad number.



Delap had been Chelsea's No.9 since signing from Ipswich Town in June 2025.

talkSPORT understands he 23-year-old is amongst the strikers under consideration for an exit despite having five years left on his deal.



Alongside Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu, Delap is available for offers before the transfer window closes.

His preference would be to remain in England for the upcoming season.

Although Italian side Como have shown interest, Delap is hopeful offers from within the Premier League emerge before the window closes.



The former England Under-21 international scored three goals in 47 appearances for Chelsea in all competitions last season.

Of those only one came in the Premier League, a consolation strike in a defeat to Fulham back in January.

3 Delap has been stripped of the No.9 shirt amid doubts over his Chelsea future Credit: Getty

Chelsea squad numbers revealed

Elsewhere, Wesley Fofana has also been handed a new squad number, inheriting the No.3 from the departed Marc Cucurella.



Fofana has previously worn both No.33 and No.29 for the Blues since signing from Leicester City four years ago.

British-record signing Morgan Rogers will wear the No.17 shirt for Xabi Alonso's side this term.

Notable former recipients include Eden Hazard, Mohamed Salah and Raheem Sterling.

3 British-record signing Rogers has been given the No.17 shirt at Stamford Bridge Credit: AFP



Chelsea 2026/27 squad numbers 1. Roberto Sanchez 2. Marco Palestra 3. Wesley Fofana 4. Valentin Barco 5. Maxence Lacroix 6. Levi Colwill 7. Pedro Neto 8. Enzo Fernandez 9. Joao Pedro 10. Cole Palmer 11. Jamie Gittens 12. Liam Delap 14. Jordan Henderson 15. Nicolas Jackson 16. Dario Essugo 17. Morgan Rogers 18. Danny Welbeck 19. Mamadou Sarr 21. Jorrel Hato 22. Emmanuel Emegha 23. Geovany Quenda 24. Reece James 25. Moises Caicedo 27. Malo Gusto 28. Teddy Sharman-Lowe 29. Pep Chavarria 30. Aaron Anselmino 31. Reggie Watson 32. Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli 33. Mykhailo Mudryk 34. Josh Acheampong 37. Tayo Subuloye 38. Tosin Adarabioyo 39. Mike Penders 41. Estevao 44. Gaga Slonina 45. Romeo Lavia

Mykailo Mudryk has also received a new number after being cleared to return to action following the resolution of his doping case.

The winger will wear the No.33 shirt this season, with his old No.10 now held by Cole Palmer.

Defender Tosin Adarabioyo no longer holds the No.4 jersey and instead has No.38. Summer signing Valentin Barco is the new No.4.

The No.38 was previously held by Guiu, who now doesn't have a number.

Chelsea begin their season away to local rivals Fulham on Monday night.



The two sides meet at Craven Cottage, with kick-off at 8pm live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish officially gets new Man City squad number after losing No.10 jersey
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish officially gets new Man City squad number after losing No.10 jersey

Jack Grealish has officially been given the No.18 shirt at Manchester City, in another hint he could be set to stay.

The forward made his first appearance for the Citizens in 453 days last weekend, as he was introduced at half time in their Community Shield defeat to Arsenal.

4 Grealish wore the No.18 in his first Man City appearance since May 2025 in the Community Shield Credit: Getty

After the match, new City boss Enzo Maresca appeared to suggest Grealish could yet have a future at the Etihad Stadium.

This comes after the England international spent last season on loan at Everton, before the Toffees opted against triggering their option to buy clause.

New beginning for Grealish?

While speculation continues over where Grealish could end up next, he remains a City player for the time being.

And the club appear to have taken steps to confirm this following his Sky Blues return in the Community Shield.

After coming on at half time in the 3-0 defeat, the 30-year-old wore the No.18 shirt in a new sight to fans.

Grealish had donned the No.10 during his City career up until his loan to Everton last season, when he lost it to Rayan Cherki.

And now the Englishman is back in Manchester, it appears he has been forced into a permanent number change.

After wearing it on his back during the Community Shield, the winger will officially wear the No.18 on his shirt this term.

Man City have confirmed this on their website, with Grealish previously appearing on their squad list without a number.

Now though, he is credited with his new number, which previously belonged to recently-departed goalkeeper Stefan Ortega.

4 Grealish was given the No.10 shirt at Man City upon arrival for a then-British record £100million fee in 2021 Credit: AFP

4 Cherki was then handed the maverick number last summer before Grealish joined Everton on loan Credit: Getty

While Ortega last donned the No.18 at the club, Fabian Delph, Frank Lampard and Gareth Barry have all also worn the digits before.

Coincidentally, Grealish wore the same number at Everton last season, though it is unclear whether it carries any sentimental value.

What is the latest on Jack Grealish?

Grealish's change in shirt number comes just days after Man City boss Maresca hinted he could feature for the side this season.

Speaking after the Community Shield, Maresca explained: "He's here with us. Until he's not here with us I'll try to help him.

"If he's here he will play games."

Grealish joined City in a £100million deal from Aston Villa back in 2021.

4 Enzo Maresca has refused to rule out a future for Grealish at the Etihad Credit: AFP

Having signed a six-year contract, his deal does not expire until the end of the season.

This has led to huge speculation he would leave the Etihad this summer, even after Everton opted not to take up the £50m buy option in his loan deal.

Their decision came after he registered one goal and six assists in 22 appearances for the Toffees, having missed the end of last season as he underwent surgery on a foot fracture in February.

talkSPORT previously reported Grealish was drawing interest from Saudi side Al Hilal, while he sent the rumour mill into overdrive when he was spotted at Wrexham's Championship opener against Cardiff on Monday.

The playmaker has made 158 appearances for Man City in all competitions, scoring 17 goals and providing 23 assists.

He has won seven major trophies including three Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen ends speculation over his F1 future by agreeing new deal with Red Bull - after four-time world champion held talks with McLaren over sensational switch
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen ends speculation over his F1 future by agreeing new deal with Red Bull - after four-time world champion held talks with McLaren over sensational switch

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Max Verstappen has ended speculation over his future by committing to remain at Red Bull until 2030 - in what could be the final deal of his Formula One career.

The four-time world champion held talks with McLaren and was linked to Mercedes over the last couple of years, but he will stay at the team where he has accrued his phenomenal success, news that is expected to be confirmed ahead of his home race in the Netherlands this weekend.

His desire to stay where he is comes after a period of negotiations that at times became fractious. His representatives were seeking an increased salary while Red Bull executives were unwilling to improve on his £60million-a-year deal. Compromise has been found to keep their star asset.

It ends conjecture over the 28-year-old's plans after he held talks with McLaren boss Zak Brown a couple of months ago.

The exact details of Verstappen's deal remain to be seen. He is already committed to Red Bull until the end of 2028.

Max Verstappen has ended speculation over his future by signing a new deal with Red Bull

The 28-year-old has committed his future until 2030, in what could be his final F1 contract

'I am really pleased with the contract extension,' Verstappen said via Red Bull Racing's official website.

'We have the best people and I'm excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again. This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue. I want to thank Red Bull, Laurent [Mekies] and everyone at Oracle Red Bull Racing for the trust they put in me.

'I have always said it: The Team is like a second family for me and I feel very at home. I came to the Team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely and we have shared many incredible moments and won four World Championships.

'To continue this journey with the same Team that I have been with my whole career is really special and something I have always wanted to do.'

Verstappen had been linked with a move to reigning champions McLaren

Mekies added: 'Having Max continue with us and retaining the best driver on the grid is fantastic news for everyone at Red Bull, Oracle Red Bull Racing, as well as F1 and motorsport as a whole.

'Very few partnerships in sport achieve what Max and this Team have. Since the very beginning, Max has embodied everything that makes Oracle Red Bull Racing special: uncompromising competitiveness, relentless determination and the courage to challenge convention.

'His impact on our Team and on Red Bull's motorsport story has been transformational, and he has been fundamental to everything we have accomplished together.'

Sports.title: British motorbike racer Sam Naughton, 37, dies in horror Manx Grand Prix qualifying crash - just one day after fellow rider was killed in fatal session
Sports.content:
British motorbike racer Sam Naughton has died during qualifying for the Manx Grand Prix, becoming the second rider killed during the fatal session this week.

The 37-year-old was taking part in the Grand Prix for just the second time, and died in a crash which took place on a western section of the island's course called Doran's Bend.

Naughton's death during the afternoon session on Wednesday came less than 24 hours after the first fatality of qualifying, with Swiss rider Mauro Poncini involved in a tragic accident on the opening lap of Tuesday evening's session.

Isle of Man native Naughton made his debut at the Grand Prix last year on the Mountain Course.

A statement released by Manx Grand Prix Races shared that the organisation was 'deeply saddened' by the racer's death.

'Having made his debut in 2025, Sam was in his second year of competing at the Manx Grand Prix, and was a regular competitor at a number of other road racing events since he began racing in 2020,' the statement continued.

Motorbike rider Sam Naughton, 37, has died during qualifying for the Manx Grand Prix

'The Manx Grand Prix Races pass on their deepest sympathy to his wife Charlotte, his children Bonnie, Liam, Jesse and Parker, his family, and friends.'

Wednesday also saw the Swiss Moto Federation pay tribute to Poncini, who was making his debut in the race when he was killed at Cruickshanks.

'Mauro was a man with an extraordinary heart, deeply affectionate toward his loved ones and everyone around him,' the statement read, adding that the federation were experiencing 'profound shock and immense sadness'.

'Thanks to his warm and open nature, he was well-loved by fellow riders and appreciated by all for his great humanity.'

Adding that he was a 'passionate and deeply committed rider' who 'lived his passion wholeheartedly, with courage and absolute dedication,' the statement added: 'Now - far too soon - that very passion has taken him to the heavens'.

Naughton is the second rider to have died at Doran's Bend this year, with British rider Daniel Ingham dying at the site during the first lap of qualifying at the Isle of Man TT in May.

Father of two Ingham, 33, had been a regular at the event since 2016, first competing in the Manx Grand Prix before swapping to TT races.

In a second incident at that event, eight spectators were taken to hospital after a rider crashed during practice.

The Isle of Man TT is generally considered one of the most dangerous races in motorsport, with Ingham's death marking the 272nd on the Snaefell Mountain Course.

Events on the course, including the Grand Prix and Classic TT races, will continue until August 28.

Sports.title: 'We tell him off if he gets carried away!': Brighton star JACK HINSHELWOOD joins dad Adam and great-uncle Martin to reflect on three generations of serving the Seagulls, the club's 'incredible' journey and his goal target for this season
Sports.content:
Jack Hinshelwood's season ended with a flourish. There were the three goals in as many games as Brighton qualified for Europe and a distinct feeling there were more where they came from.

Hinshelwood, having first broken into the team at full back and played deep in midfield, has thrived as a high-energy No 10 in Fabian Hurzeler's side, forcing errors from those trying to pass their way out of defence and latching onto crosses to threaten the goal.

Thomas Tuchel liked what he saw and selected the 21-year-old in England's 55-man longlist for the World Cup. Wealthy Premier League rivals monitored his accelerated progress, too.

Summer speculation about interest from Arsenal sparked flattering online comparisons to David Platt, the former England captain with a reputation for scoring goals from midfield.

'If I'm going to play in this higher position, I want to start scoring a few more goals,' Hinshelwood tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I scored four last season but could have had 15 so I'm working hard to turn good positioning into more goals and assists. I want to score 10-plus if we're going to play 50-60 games.

'There's a lot to play for this season. We're in the Conference League, which is a massive target for us. We really want to do well in Europe. We'll be better prepared than two years ago. We want to go as far as we can, like in every competition.'

Hinshelwood discusses his ambitions under the critical gaze of his father Adam, a former Brighton player now manager of Worthing in the National League, and his great-uncle Martin, who has served Brighton in several coaching roles including as manager and director of football, and still scouts for the club.

Jack Hinshelwood, his father Adam (right) and great-uncle Martin (left) have all served Brighton with distinction as either a player or coach

The trio met Daily Mail Sport at Brighton Museum and Art Gallery, for the opening of a permanent exhibition tracing the history of the club

A talented and versatile player, Jack is entering his fourth season with the Brighton first team and has been touted for an England call-up

For all his confidence, Jack qualifies everything with regular promises not to look 'too far ahead' and to 'focus on Brighton' and let the rest take care of itself. His family background guards naturally against the dangers of getting carried away.

'He'll get told off by the rest of us if he does,' teases Martin but his expert eye tells him his great-nephew has the attributes required to turn this excellent start into an elite career.

'You're in a learning curve and it's a massive bonus if you're able to play in different areas of the pitch with the ability and the will to play there, because I know some players will go, "What you playing me there for? I don't want to play there. I want to play in that position".'

Martin expects Jack will eventually settle into central midfield. 'His awareness is his big asset,' says the 73-year-old. 'He knows where he is on the pitch and where others are. He sees things and does things early. He's just an intelligent footballer, probably more intelligent than any of the rest of us who have played.'

Three generations of the Hinshelwood family are together at Brighton Museum and Art Gallery for the opening of a permanent exhibition tracing the history of the club, and especially its revival since the closure of the Goldstone Ground amid fears of liquidation in 1997, from exile in Gillingham to success in the Premier League.

'The journey has been incredible,' says Jack, whose introduction came as an infant at the Withdean athletics complex where Brighton played home games after returning to the city in 1999. His father was in the team.

Likewise, Adam's early recollections include splashing around with his cousins in the huge communal baths inside the Goldstone dressing rooms when Martin worked on the staff. And later as ball boy at the Withdean as the team started its climb back to the top.

Martin, Adam and Jack have been witnesses to Brighton's 'incredible' journey from near extinction to European football

Jack is honoured alongside fellow Brighton fan favourites in the exhibition covering that revival

Brighton's former Withdean ground was a distinctive venue for football, with an athletics track around the pitch

'There was a buzz when the team came back to play in Brighton and Hove,' says Adam, 42. 'And there were back-to-back promotions and before you knew it the Withdean was a Championship ground hosting some big teams.

'It was layered differently to normal grounds. The players' lounge was a nursery by day and there was a pub literally inside the ground. Now they're building a pub inside the Amex so it'll bring some history back.'

The Hinshelwoods are woven into the club's fabric.

Adam, who is the son of Crystal Palace legend Paul, was thrust into the Brighton first team at the age of 18, making his debut on the opening day of the 2002-03 campaign when his uncle Martin was manager.

He was voted man of the match in a win at Burnley and then dropped for the next game. There was a call-up by England Under 21s but no cap before his progress was halted by a serious knee injury and he retired by the age of 26.

'My career was similar to Martin's,' says Adam. 'Dad would always tell me how good Martin was as a central midfielder who could do everything, score goals, create goals and stop goals.

'His career was cut short and he got into coaching and management, and I've been fortunate to do the same. We've been on the same path. That's why I've told Jack to do his coaching badges. He's working towards his UEFA B licence.'

'He's just an intelligent footballer,' says Martin of Jack. 'Probably more intelligent than any of the rest of us who has played'

Jack's dad Adam played over 100 games for Brighton between 2002 and 2009

Martin and Paul were sons of Wally Hinshelwood who played for seven clubs, most notably Reading and Bristol City in the 1950s.

They both graduated from the youth ranks at Crystal Palace in an exciting era when Malcolm Allison and Terry Venables were in charge at Selhurst Park.

Martin's professional playing career was curtailed by injury at the age of 24. Paul went on to make 319 appearances over 10 years at Palace, mostly as a right back despite starting out as a striker.

'Paul had that attitude,' recalls Martin. 'He was a striker who scored lots of goals and when they put him at right back he wasn't too keen, but he worked hard and ended up playing for England Under-21s.'

One of his two Under-21 caps came at the Goldstone, where his every touch was booed by a partisan Brighton crowd on a night when local hero Peter Ward scored three in a 6-0 win against Norway.

'There's no magic to it,' says Martin, as he attempts to explain the dynasty with a story about his father's matter-of-fact reaction to his release by Fulham at the age of 15.

'I came all the way home from Putney on my own. Train, bus, in through the front door and he went: "Are they taking you as an apprentice, then?" I said, "No". And he said: "You're probably not good enough". Then you think: "Well, I'll show you".

'My parents helped us in every way but always left a bit there to say, "Go on, you need to do more". That's how it's got to be or you can have a problem. I had that as a kid and Adam had that with his dad as well.

'They'd always find something in the game and go, "Hey, remember that?". You might have had a blinder, but they'd forget all the good things and remind you about that one thing. It's just to keep your feet on the ground and keep you wanting to improve and be a better person and player.'

Having played for rivals Crystal Palace, Martin stepped in as Brighton's caretaker manager on several occasions in the 2000s

'None of us are comfortable with what we've got,' says Jack. 'Like Dad in his coaching, he's doing really well but we all want more. It never stops'

As coaches with family in football, Martin and Adam find themselves doing the same thing.

'My youngest son is 11 and he probably gets it a lot easier than Jack did,' says Adam. 'When I started, I had my uncle coaching at Brighton and he'd shout to me: "Hinsh, are you all right?" and I'd say, "Yeah" and he'd say, "Liven up then". That would get to me every time.'

Jack has no complaints about the extra scrutiny. 'None of us are comfortable with what we've got,' he says. 'Like Dad in his coaching, he's doing really well but we all want more. It never stops.

'And probably that means we don't enjoy it sometimes as we should, but we always just want more.'

Brighton's new season starts tonight with a Conference League play-off tie against Tromso in Norway, before they host Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday. Expect more from young Hinshelwood.

Sports.title: 'He's not in it for the money': Insiders reveal the real reasons why football sceptic Jeff Bezos has bought into Liverpool - as well as his plans for his 'new toy', why Reds' commercial income will explode and angry fan groups' next steps
Sports.content:
There's an old and barely documented story about Jeff Bezos that is worth excavating for a single reason – the yarn is the only one to suggest Liverpool’s newest shareholder held even a passing interest in sport as a child.

It dates to when Bezos, 62, was aged nine and living in Houston. As the mother to a bookish, scrawny lad, Jacklyn Bezos thought her boy needed to toughen up, which meant shifting him from his comfort zones of Star Trek and studying.

This would have been around 1973 and American football was the means to an end Jacklyn chose. In Texas, that is no small undertaking, so Jacklyn had her worries. ‘I thought he was going to get creamed out there,’ she said in the buried sections of an interview published by Wired in 1999.

Naturally, the profile didn’t conclude with a punchline about violent defeat. Instead, as Bezos’s late mother recalled it, the future founder of Amazon was the only child on the side capable of memorising all the plays. Not only his plays, but those of all his team-mates, too. She claimed he was made captain of the defence in the space of two weeks.

It’s a fun snippet but difficult to corroborate – Daily Mail Sport has trawled the archives of Houston’s multiple local newspapers from that period and found no mention of a ‘Coach Meisner’, which was among the few tangible details when the Washington Post – which Bezos now owns – repeated the anecdote in 2000. Emails to a couple of American football historians in Texas also proved fruitless.

If the story teaches us anything, it is the rarity of finding the young Bezos in any athletic environment whatsoever.

Jeff Bezos (pictured with his wife Lauren Sanchez), the world's third richest man, is part of a consortium that have bought almost 40 per cent of Liverpool

There is little evidence Bezos has any passion for sport, much less football - so why has he bought into Liverpool?

A young Bezos was encouraged by his mother to play American football in a bid to toughen him up - but we can't find any records of his sporting exploits

When Daily Mail Sport contacted his former school, Palmetto High in Miami, it required only six minutes to establish that the most famous of their alumni from the class of 82 never kicked, threw, jumped, swam, ran or sailed for any of its teams.

Wade Rowdon, once a third baseman at Cincinnati Reds and three years ahead of Bezos at Palmetto, told me he only recently found out they attended the same school – Bezos may have changed the world of retail forever but, evidently, he never left even the faintest of sporting footprints on his own playground.

All of which means nothing and something, because there are important questions to be asked of the ‘why’ whenever a financial behemoth lays hands on a sporting institution, and a deep-seated passion for the property at hand is often the first to be ruled out. In the case of Liverpool FC and its union with the world’s third richest man, that can be taken as a given.

A week has passed since Liverpool’s owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) announced a ‘definitive agreement’ had been reached for a consortium named 1892 Holdings to buy a ‘minority’ stake in the club at the heart of a socialist city.

It has since transpired that the slice of the pie they have bought for more than £2billion is significantly bigger than initially reported – closer to 38 or 39 per cent rather than 30 per cent – and that options exist for 1892 to assume a majority shareholding within 12 months.

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to figures involved in the deal, financial experts and supporter groups concerned about the implications. But among the bigger mysteries within all of it is Bezos, a man worth £194.9billion, according to Forbes’ real-time listings on Wednesday morning.

Based on our conversations with individuals connected to the negotiations, Bezos was not on the frontline of talks, nor anywhere especially close. That role was taken by Amit Bhatia, the former co-owner of QPR and son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal.

We understand Bhatia first met with FSG president Mike Gordon a year ago, after introductions from Will McDonough, the founder of Corestone Capital and a former agent to NFL legend Tom Brady. Interestingly, McDonough was also a senior adviser to the White House task force at this summer’s World Cup.

It was during the World Cup that FSG founder John W Henry is understood to have met Bhatia at an elite private members’ club in New York, Zero Bond, with the deal having moved quickly over the summer. ‘The past three months is when it all escalated,’ a source from the consortium told Daily Mail Sport.

Former QPR vice-chairman Amit Bhatia has been the face of the 1892 consortium, holding meetings with FSG president Mike Gordon a year ago

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is also attached to the group, through his wife Elaine

It is well known by now that Bhatia will be abundantly visible as the vice-chair of the new Liverpool, pending approval of the acquisition by the independent regulator, and two more board seats will go to members of the 1892 consortium – Elaine Saverin, the wife of Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, and Bryan Baum, who is the managing partner of K5 Global.

Bezos, the lead investor in K5, is conspicuous in that he holds no precise role and will instead hover as an unseen force in the background.

Our sources characterised him distinctly as a ‘silent partner’ and K5 is yet to reply to multiple Daily Mail Sport requests for clarity on the precise size of his investment, with K5 said to have pumped $1billion into the consortium’s coffers. With that level of attachment, it is safe to assume that if Bezos wishes to pull a string at the club, the absence of a designated board seat would be little more than a furniture issue.

And yet the opaque nature of his involvement, and a perceived lack of transparency around the wider process, is part of the uncertainty that has brought some anxiety to the fanbase.

Daily Mail Sport has been told the influential supporter group Spirit of Shankly (SoS) will hold a meeting with the regulator next week to share a few of those thoughts, which are inevitably tethered to memories of the despised ownership of George Gillett and Tom Hicks, which preceded FSG.

A spokesperson for SoS told Daily Mail Sport on Tuesday: ‘We want to know what it all means for Liverpool. We know firsthand what it's like to have bad ownership, so we want to know how the club will be run and by whom.’

The same spokesperson got in touch on Wednesday, after it emerged in The Athletic that the stake was closer to 40 per cent, adding: ‘The fact we didn’t know the percentage has given us more questions to ask. It has changed the landscape – this is not a small investment and we need to know more about what it means for the club.’

There is some reading to be done between the lines here. Change can be good, of course, and there is no one so blind as to assume FSG have lacked mis-steps since taking over for £300million in 2010 – they were part of the grubby posse that tried for a Super League breakaway and have pushed for an assortment of unpopular price hikes.

But FSG, while overseeing multiple sporting victories from their base in Boston, have also shown, on occasion, a willingness to listen to public backlashes, notably after the fury that erupted around their plans to raise ticket prices this year. The fans forced a rethink, but it’s a dynamic that cannot be guaranteed with new faces – the jokes about discussing supporter issues with an Amazon chatbot will no doubt write themselves.

Sources involved in the 1892 deal have stressed that they will engage the supporters, but said those conversations will likely occur after the regulator has approved the purchase. The intervening wait of up to 90 days could supply a vacuum for fraught sentiments, especially as Premier League and UEFA spending rules mean the era of free-spending on popular new signings are over.

Bezos has only ever been spotted at one football match - USA's defeat by Belgium at the World Cup last month

Liverpool fan group Spirit of Shankly, who protested the club's involvement in the Super League under FSG, want answers around the nature of Bezos' investment

Quite why Bezos is investing in Liverpool is both obvious and difficult to decipher. Returns in the best-case scenario would be pocket change to a man of his wealth, but iconic sporting properties are hard to acquire. By extension, they are attractive.

After backing away from explored purchases of the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders in 2019 and 2023 respectively, Liverpool is Bezos’s entry point to an alien world.

It is understood that he hasn’t yet stepped foot inside Anfield and his appearance, alongside his wife Lauren Sanchez, at Team USA’s World Cup defeat by Belgium in Seattle last month is the only clear evidence of him ever attending a match. The assumption of Kieran Maguire, the noted football finance expert, is that Liverpool will serve as something akin to a fancy new toy, which might tally with the separate impression that Bezos has grown fonder of a celebrity lifestyle in the past decade.

‘Bezos isn't in it for the money because even if he makes $500million out of this himself, it's not going to move the dial for him,’ Maguire told me.

‘It’s about the kudos, I think. It's about being able to own a room in a different way at a cocktail party. Everybody in that set has an apartment in Manhattan, a yacht, there's only 20 football clubs in the Premier League and there's only one Liverpool. It could just be a hobby, a trophy asset.’

That might serve as scant comfort for Liverpool fans, who will be cognisant that the presence of Bezos is no guarantee of success – masses of discarded staff from the Washington Post prove that point.

But Maguire does foresee key areas of potential for Liverpool from the wider alliance, especially as a means of capitalising on the rapid, recent growth of Indian interest in the Premier League.

‘Longer term, what are Liverpool looking for?’ Maguire asks. ‘They're looking to expand into international markets under the cost-control rules and where are the growth opportunities? Answer A is the United States. Well, hello, Jeff Bezos. And answer B is India. Hello, Mr Mittal (whose family trust is named alongside Bhatia in the purchase).

‘I think there is the opportunity there to use the knowledge of those individuals to enable Liverpool to extract further commercial income, to tap into their networks, to tap into their expertise.

‘As for Bezos personally, my gut reaction is that it’s a vanity purchase, but as a secondary thought, he will want to expand Amazon into new markets and having an involvement with an iconic club will help.’

'It's about being able to own a room at a cocktail party. Everybody in that set has an apartment in Manhattan, a yacht, but there's only one Liverpool'

Time will tell if that leads one day to Amazon sponsorship on the shirt or stadium wall – sources in the deal claim it was not part of the current thinking. We also understand there is no concern from the Premier League or UEFA about perceived conflicts of interest around Amazon Prime’s ownership of broadcasting rights to football. Precedents already exist in that area.

That said, there is a mild curiosity, expressed by one figure near the top of British football, about whether this involvement might encourage Bezos to put extra effort into tackling rights piracy, which is often linked to modified Amazon Fire Sticks.

For now, that is an unknown. So too is the question of whether Bezos might be faced with a rush of cancelled subscriptions if results go badly or fans dislike what they discover.

It might not go in that direction, of course, but football can be funny like that. Presumably Bezos has learned as much in his due diligence, because 53 years after he pulled on pads for a kids’ team, there are myriad ways he could still get creamed.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has been set up to fail by Ineos - but it's not the first time he's been let down by his bosses. This is the proof he's the perfect manager for Man United's threadbare squad
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has been set up to fail by Ineos - but it's not the first time he's been let down by his bosses. This is the proof he's the perfect manager for Man United's threadbare squad

Unlock more from our team inside the Man United camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

When Michael Carrick’s star was in its ascendancy at Middlesbrough, with first-season performances at places like Sheffield United and Burnley which were described as ‘near perfection’ creating a genuine prospect of promotion to the Premier League, he was being compared by some to Keanu Reeves' character in The Matrix. A quiet and immensely self-possessed individual using all his mental faculties to navigate a manic universe.

He likes to say that being a former midfielder influences the way he coaches – it’s not all blood and thunder with him – and if one word encapsulates the way he worked on Teesside, then it is ‘calm’.

But his mentor Sir Alex Ferguson once said that there are times in football management where ‘you have to stand up for yourself – there is no other way’. Carrick’s disinclination to do that struck many at the start of a second season at the Middlesbrough helm, as he struggled to live up to the big reputation he had built in his first.

No fewer than 14 senior players had left in that summer’s transfer window, including forwards Chuba Akpom and Cameron Archer, as Boro ended a heavy dependency on loan signings.

Carrick, left to assimilate new recruits and build a new team on the hoof for a fanbase expecting another promotion push, was plunged into undoubtedly his toughest period in football. Boro picked up two points from their winless first seven games and after a desultory Tuesday night draw at Sheffield Wednesday – where they trailed at half-time – sat rock bottom.

Those bleak, winless months looked like second season syndrome – a time, if ever there was one, for him to speak up, defend himself and send a veiled message ‘upstairs’. Nothing of the sort was forthcoming, as Carrick, steadfastly disinclined to use the press conference sphere for his own purposes as Ferguson always would, remained a rock-solid company man.

Man United's lack of transfer business means Michael Carrick has been set up to fail before a ball has even been kicked this season

But Carrick has been here before going into his second season - he lost 14 senior players in the equivalent summer at Middlesbrough, including star striker Chuba Akpom (second from right)

As he prepares Manchester United for the new campaign, Carrick does not have another full-scale rebuild on his hands, but he is once again entitled to feel the sting of indignation about how he is being sent into a second season by his employers.

The landscape is wholly different to his first United season, with the return of Champions League football likely to mean United will play 15 games more. Yet to date, they have just two significant additions to what was already a thin squad: Youri Tielemans, a 29-year-old with many miles on the clock, and Andrey Santos, a recruit from Chelsea nowhere near the finished article.

Ahead of Saturday’s opening game at Hull, Carrick has the same old dependency on Luke Shaw, who is nowhere near capable of playing the two games per week which European football demands, and the other defensive old-stager Harry Maguire.

Matthijs de Ligt has not played a game since last November. Lisandro Martinez is recovering from a thigh problem after an injury-ravaged last season. Benjamin Sesko has not kicked a ball in pre-season. There is, as yet, no one new to energise a midfield from which Casemiro has gone and Manuel Ugarte will be missing most of the season. United have a lower summer spend than Ipswich Town and Coventry City.

It feels like Carrick is being set up to fail before a ball is even kicked, with some analysts already inferring that he is not the man to take United on. Jamie Carragher recently suggested that he lacks the ‘stardust’ to win them a Premier League or Champions League title.

Having rescued United from the humiliating position that the club’s owners, Ineos, found themselves in after begging the incapable and tempestuous Ruben Amorim to leave Sporting Lisbon to manage their club, Carrick deserves much better. Yet for all that, the evidence of the pre-season tells us that he is the same safe, dependable guy who didn't make waves at Middlesbrough.

If you looked hard enough, there were signs of a man trying to send a message that he needed more players, as he sat in a hotel meeting room with national print journalists at Manchester United’s hotel in County Kildare after the recent friendly against Leeds United. ‘We've got to keep pushing, really, and push everything in every boundary that we can, to be able to win again,’ he said.

But he’s agreed to Amazon camera crews being around the club for a United documentary series – something no United manager before him would ever have countenanced, least of all Amorim, with his predilection for punching TVs.

Carrick's options for Saturday's game against Hull are far from ideal - striker Benjamin Sesko, for example, has not featured throughout pre-season

United still depend on left back Luke Shaw, who is nowhere near capable of playing the two games per week which European football demands

He’s said it’s acceptable that United, whose commercial revenues are the second highest in world football, won’t pursue £100million players, despite the club being the only one of the ‘Big Six’ not to have done so. He hasn’t even brought up the question of the season’s significantly greater workload.

While some afford Carrick the public indignities they would be less willing to submit a foreign manager to, the Manchester United faithful are desperate for him to be the one who brings the club out of the post-Ferguson purgatory.

Ineos and their United chief executive Omar Berrada have made grand boasts about ‘Project 150’ – winning or challenging for the Premier League by the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028 – which will come back to bite fans if unaccomplished. Ineos, not Carrick, will be on the receiving end of supporters’ opprobrium if this becomes another turbulent season.

For the many who want to see Carrick flourish, there is evidence from that second Middlesbrough season of how his understated and thoughtful approach might just deliver.

Those who viewed him at close quarters still remember that steadfast loyalty to the owners. ‘There was never any sign of him rocking the boat,’ says Dominic Shaw, who covers the club for The Northern Echo. ‘Even through that winless stretch, he went nowhere near suggesting, “I don’t yet have the squad”.’

Asked before leaving Hillsborough, on the nadir of a night which kept them bottom, what he had told his players at half-time, Carrick inevitably replied: ‘I kept calm.’ But many of the players who came through the difficult early months to find success and finish eighth in that 2023-24 season speak of how his application to the small details of their technique made them better players, in the eye of that storm.

Morgan Rogers, who’d struggled to convince in a number of loan moves when he arrived at Boro in July 2023, spoke when eventually called up by England of how Carrick had been a ‘massive part’ in his own development. ‘He gave me the confidence to express myself.’

Carrick called him to thank him for these words but told him: ‘Don't play down how much you've done yourself.’ For Rogers, management, in the purest sense of the word, had clearly mattered more than that amorphous ‘stardust’ quality which pundits speak of. Humility is a part of it. It’s thought that Carrick did not try to bring his own decorated playing career into his conversations with Rogers.

England star and Chelsea summer signing Morgan Rogers credits Carrick as being a 'massive part' of his development

It felt significant in a recent County Kildare discussion with journalists that Carrick did not take the chance offered to him to say he felt ‘empathy’ for Marcus Rashford

Rogers would repay Boro with a £15million profit in his move to Aston Villa, having dazzled in the club’s run to the Carabao Cup semi-final. Emmanuel Latte Lath, also signed that summer, turned out to be the Championship’s striker of the season and Rav van den Berg, now playing in the Bundesliga, proved an excellent centre back. Boro eventually profited to the tune of around £50million from that summer's buys.

A source who knows Lath tells of how Carrick managed to drop the striker to the bench without jolting the confidence which so many forwards feed off. Van den Berg speaks of Carrick’s ‘understanding’ of what it was taking to adjust to the Championship.

Carrick’s presence on a Zoom call had been instrumental to him signing. Yet there was clearly an uncompromising side to him on Teesside. ‘It was not all sweetness and light. It’s a hard game and his dressing room reflected that,’ says the source close to Lath.

It felt significant in the County Kildare discussion with journalists that Carrick did not take the chance offered to him to say he felt ‘empathy’ for Marcus Rashford. Perhaps this was Carrick code for ‘grow up and sort yourself out’. But all the soundings suggest he is ready to give the forward the fresh start Amorim would not countenance for the England international.

Carrick’s tone seemed different when it came to Kobbie Mainoo, another cast to the margins by Amorim. He and Mainoo have been in touch on and off throughout his frustrating summer with England. Carrick didn’t discuss Amad Diallo in Ireland but he is another young United player thought to feel reinvigorated. Echoes of that Boro cohort.

Carrick’s most questionable act at Middlesbrough was a decision to replace first-team coach Aaron Danks with his own brother Graeme, previously the Newcastle United Under 18s coach, when Danks left to join Vincent Kompany at Bayern Munich.

But the appointment of Danks, within two months of his own appointment, did underline Carrick’s ability to assemble a good ‘brains trust’. At United, Steve Holland has become the same problem-solver and shrewd tactician with answers that Gareth Southgate always found him to be with England.

Carrick was aware from day one that the fragility in this United group was borne of the chaotic changes Amorim would make, half an hour before kick-off. Holland is there to make sure everything is clear. Jonathan Woodgate and Jonny Evans, who make up the coaching team, are popular. It is the strongest and most united backroom team for many seasons.

Carrick left Teesside with a reputation for predictability: being bound to an aesthetically pleasing pass-and-move style with ‘only one distinct way of playing’ as Sunderland’s extremely adaptable and dynamic manager Regis Le Bris brutally described the team down the A19 after beating them in 2024.

Carrick left Teesside with a reputation for predictability: being bound to an aesthetically pleasing pass-and-move style with ‘only one distinct way of playing’

But United's pursuit of the tough defensive midfielder Carlos Baleba (right) suggests Carrick has learned from his mistakes

‘They were not as streetwise as they needed to be,’ says the Northern Echo’s Shaw. ‘Being unable to see games out was a repeated problem and there was also a sequence of conceding shambolic goals through poor defending.’

There is evidence that Carrick has learned from that experience, too. The pursuit of tough central and defensive midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton would, if it comes off, suggest a big shift from his old aesthetic.

The season ahead will bring United up against some of those players Carrick mentored so well at Middlesbrough. They will face Morgan Rogers at Chelsea, two months from now. Akpom, transformed in Carrick's first season, is on the fringes of the Ipswich side the team meet a week on Sunday.

Sitting back in that hotel meeting room to discuss the season ahead, the United manager pointedly dodged the question of whether his side can challenge for the title.

‘What we've done gives us the confidence to move forward. How quickly we keep moving forward, that's the challenge – but as long as we're stable and we can keep moving in the direction, I think that's what we can ask,' he stated.

He was as calm, unflustered and equable as always, but will need every ounce of skill to tackle the Matrix which lies ahead this time.

Sports.title: Inside the explosive WhatsApps about alleged Sydney Swans hotel incident: What's NOT true in texts and graphic photo going viral
Sports.content:
Inside the explosive WhatsApps about alleged Sydney Swans hotel incident: What's NOT true in texts and graphic photo going viral

What we know about the texts, what's alleged, what's already been disproven

Inside the rumours engulfing the Swans before finals

Do you know more? Email: lucy.manly@dailymail.com.au

Sydney Swans WAGs appear to be battening down the hatches after the alleged hotel incident engulfing the team just days out from the AFL finals.

Isaac Heeney's fiancée Steffanie Waters and Chad Warner's long-term girlfriend Alice Hughes have both made telling changes to their social media accounts following the explosive allegations.

Heeney appears to have switched off comments on his Instagram account, while his bride-to-be has disabled comments on most posts.

Ms Waters' profile remains public, however, which is perhaps unsurprising given her career as an influencer.

Warner's girlfriend Ms Hughes, a Perth-raised nurse who moved to Sydney after the midfielder was drafted by the Swans, has made her Instagram account private.

The social media lockdown comes as the club finds itself at the centre of a police investigation just days before the AFL finals.

Isaac Heeney's fiancée Steffanie Waters disabled comments for most posts on her Instagram

It is possible that Waters' account only remains public due to her work as an influencer

Chad Warner voluntarily spoke with police about the allegations but was not arrested. He is pictured here with his long-term girlfriend Alice Hughes

The Swans were celebrating a crucial 36-point victory over Essendon at the MCG on Sunday, a result which cemented second spot on the ladder and booked them a home qualifying final at the SCG.

But by Monday morning, the mood had dramatically changed.

Victoria Police attended the Pullman East Melbourne hotel, where the Swans had been staying, following a report of an alleged sexual assault in the early hours of the morning.

And amid the police investigation, a series of questionable WhatsApp messages purporting to reveal what unfolded inside the Melbourne hotel have been doing the rounds online.

The messages, which the Mail has not been able to independently authenticate, make a string of extraordinary claims about the events that allegedly took place after the Swans' victory on Sunday.

However, key inconsistencies raise serious doubts about the authenticity and veracity of the texts.

According to the messages, Warner, Heeney, Riley Bice, James Jordon and a fifth unnamed player were 'all in custody'.

However, this cannot be true because the players were not arrested, voluntarily offered their assistance to the police investigation, and returned to Sydney via rental car.

Victoria Police attended the Pullman East Melbourne hotel (pictured), where the Swans had been staying, following a report of an alleged sexual assault in the early hours of the morning

The unverified messages make a string of extraordinary claims about the events that allegedly took place after the Swans' victory on Sunday. The players were not arrested and were able to leave the state and return to Sydney via rental car

An unauthenticated text purports to show an image from inside the Pullman hotel

A photo circulating online has already been debunked as a fake

One bizarre message alleges how a woman was injured in the room, with a photo offered as evidence. However, that image has already been debunked as a fake taken months ago.

Screenshots of the texts also make wild and entirely unverified claims of a woman taunting a player with insects, only for an argument to erupt, causing damage to the hotel, while another player allegedly took bets on the ensuing chaos.

There is no evidence to suggest this account of the incident is true.
